headlines.title: Brent crude tops $108 after Saudi Arabia shuts down critical pipeline that bypasses Strait of Hormuz
headlines.summary: This is the tape-mover of the week — Brent north of $108 with the East-West pipeline offline means the Strait of Hormuz is now the only game in town for Saudi exports, and the market knows it. Energy names, airlines, trucking, and anything with a fuel bill are all in play, while the broader equity complex gets hit with a stagflation scare right before the Fed meeting. JPMorgan's strategists are already flagging a swift decline risk, and they're not wrong to sweat it.

headlines.title: Stocks Slide as AI Slowdown Fears Hit Sentiment: Markets Wrap
headlines.summary: When the biggest names in AI — Altman, Amodei, Musk — all stand up and say 'pump the brakes,' the market listens, because AI capex has been the engine driving the whole tech rally. Nvidia, the hyperscalers, the data center REITs — every name that rode the AI wave is now staring at potential earnings revision risk, and Citi is already waving the red flag. This isn't a one-day story; if the pause talk gains traction in Washington, the multiple compression could be ugly.

headlines.title: A 5% Treasury Yield Raises New Risks for Markets, Economy
headlines.summary: The long bond knocking on 5% is the kind of thing that keeps CFOs and portfolio managers up at night — it reprices everything from mortgage rates to equity valuations, and it's happening right as the Fed is about to make a call with oil already on fire. Bessent dared the bond market to blink and it didn't; now the question is whether the Fed hikes into an oil shock or watches yields do the tightening for them. Either way, rate-sensitive sectors — utilities, REITs, homebuilders — are in the crosshairs.
